sanskrit: dattvātithibhyo devebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svajanasya ca avaśiṣṭāni ye 'śnanti tān āhur vighasāśinaḥ
english: Those who eat what remains after they have first given to guests, to the gods, to the ancestors, and to their own kin—these are called the eaters of the leavings, the vighasāśins.

sanskrit: tasmāt svadharmam āsthāya suvratāḥ satyavādinaḥ lokasya guravo bhūtvā te bhavanty anupaskṛtāḥ
english: Therefore, abiding in their own duty, firm in their vows and truthful in speech, having become the teachers of the world, they remain unblemished and undefiled.

sanskrit: tridivaṃ prāpya śakrasya svargaloke vimatsarāḥ vasanti śāśvatīr varṣā janā duṣkarakāriṇaḥ
english: Reaching the third heaven, the celestial realm of Śakra, free from all envy, those who perform deeds hard to perform dwell there for everlasting years.

sanskrit: tatas te tad vacaḥ śrutvā tasya dharmārthasaṃhitam utsṛjya nāstikagatiṃ gārhasthyaṃ dharmam āśritāḥ
english: Then, having heard his words fraught with righteousness and worldly gain, they abandoned the path of the unbelievers and took refuge in the duty of the householder's life.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api durdharṣa dhairyam ālambya śāśvatam praśādhi pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ hatāmitrāṃ narottama
english: Therefore you too, O unassailable one, taking hold of an unwavering steadiness, govern the whole earth now that her enemies are slain, O best of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca arjunasya vacaḥ śrutvā nakulo vākyam abravīt rājānam abhisaṃprekṣya sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ varam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Arjuna, Nakula spoke, gazing upon the king, that foremost of all upholders of duty.

sanskrit: anurudhya mahāprājño bhrātuś cittam ariṃdamaḥ vyūḍhorasko mahābāhus tāmrāsyo mitabhāṣitā
english: Deferring to his brother's mind, that subduer of foes, deeply wise, broad-chested and mighty-armed, his face coppery and his speech measured, spoke thus.

sanskrit: viśākhayūpe devānāṃ sarveṣām agnayaś citāḥ tasmād viddhi mahārāja devān karmapathi sthitān
english: At the sacrificial post of Viśākhayūpa the fires of all the gods were kindled; know therefore, O great king, that the gods themselves abide on the path of ritual action.

sanskrit: anāstikān āstikānāṃ prāṇadāḥ pitaraś ca ye te 'pi karmaiva kurvanti vidhiṃ paśyasva pārthiva vedavādāpaviddhāṃs tu tān viddhi bhṛśanāstikān
english: The ancestors, the givers of life to the faithful, are themselves no unbelievers; they too perform action alone—behold this ordinance, O lord of the earth. But those who reject the teachings of the Veda, know them to be unbelievers in the extreme.

sanskrit: na hi vedoktam utsṛjya vipraḥ sarveṣu karmasu devayānena nākasya pṛṣṭham āpnoti bhārata
english: For the brāhmaṇa who casts aside what the Veda has declared in all his works does not attain the summit of heaven by the path of the gods, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: atyāśramān ayaṃ sarvān ity āhur vedaniścayāḥ brāhmaṇāḥ śrutisaṃpannās tān nibodha janādhipa
english: There are those who transcend all the orders of life, so say the brāhmaṇas learned in scripture and certain in their grasp of the Veda; mark them well, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: vittāni dharmalabdhāni kratumukhyeṣv avāsṛjan kṛtātmasu mahārāja sa vai tyāgī smṛto naraḥ
english: He who pours forth his wealth righteously gained upon the foremost of sacrifices and upon men of disciplined soul—that man, O great king, is remembered as a true renouncer.

sanskrit: anavekṣya sukhādānaṃ tathaivordhvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ ātmatyāgī mahārāja sa tyāgī tāmasaḥ prabho
english: But he who, heedless of his own well-being and grounded only in what lies beyond, casts away his very self—that self-renouncer, O great king, is a renouncer steeped in dark inertia, O lord.

sanskrit: aniketaḥ paripatan vṛkṣamūlāśrayo muniḥ apācakaḥ sadā yogī sa tyāgī pārtha bhikṣukaḥ
english: The sage who is homeless and wandering, taking shelter at the roots of trees, kindling no cooking fire, ever absorbed in yoga—that mendicant, O Pārtha, is a renouncer.

sanskrit: krodhaharṣāv anādṛtya paiśunyaṃ ca viśāṃ pate vipro vedān adhīte yaḥ sa tyāgī gurupūjakaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa who, disregarding anger and elation and slander alike, O lord of peoples, studies the Vedas and honours his teacher—he is a renouncer.

sanskrit: āśramāṃs tulayā sarvān dhṛtān āhur manīṣiṇaḥ ekatas te trayo rājan gṛhasthāśrama ekataḥ
english: The wise declare that all the orders of life are held even upon a balance: on one side, O king, stand the three orders together, and on the other the household life alone.

sanskrit: samīkṣate tu yo 'rthaṃ vai kāmaṃ svargaṃ ca bhārata ayaṃ panthā maharṣīṇām iyaṃ lokavidāṃ gatiḥ
english: He who keeps in view worldly gain, desire, and heaven alike, O descendant of Bharata—this is the path of the great sages, this the course of those who know the worlds.

sanskrit: iti yaḥ kurute bhāvaṃ sa tyāgī bharatarṣabha na yaḥ parityajya gṛhān vanam eti vimūḍhavat
english: He who shapes his disposition thus is the true renouncer, O bull of the Bharatas—not he who abandons his home and goes to the forest like one bewildered.

sanskrit: yadā kāmān samīkṣeta dharmavaitaṃsiko 'nṛjuḥ athainaṃ mṛtyupāśena kaṇṭhe badhnāti mṛtyurāṭ
english: When the crooked man who hunts the snare of righteousness merely to gratify his desires looks upon those desires, then the king of death binds him by the throat with the noose of death.

sanskrit: abhimānakṛtaṃ karma naitat phalavad ucyate tyāgayuktaṃ mahārāja sarvam eva mahāphalam
english: Action done out of pride is said to bear no fruit; but joined with renunciation, O great king, every deed yields a mighty fruit.

sanskrit: śamo damas tapo dānaṃ satyaṃ śaucam athārjavam yajño dhṛtiś ca dharmaś ca nityam ārṣo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Tranquillity, restraint, austerity, giving, truth, purity, and uprightness, sacrifice, fortitude, and righteousness—this is remembered as the eternal ordinance of the sages.

sanskrit: pitṛdevātithikṛte samārambho 'tra śasyate atraiva hi mahārāja trivargaḥ kevalaṃ phalam
english: Herein the undertaking made for the sake of the ancestors, the gods, and guests is praised; for here alone, O great king, the threefold aim of life is the entire fruit.

sanskrit: etasmin vartamānasya vidhau vipraniṣevite tyāginaḥ prasṛtasyeha nocchittir vidyate kva cit
english: For the renouncer who treads this ordinance practised by the brāhmaṇas, who goes forward upon it, there is found no ruin anywhere at all.

sanskrit: asṛjad dhi prajā rājan prajāpatir akalmaṣaḥ māṃ yakṣyantīti śāntātmā yajñair vividhadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: For Prajāpati, the stainless one of tranquil soul, brought forth creatures, O king, thinking, 'They shall worship me with sacrifices of manifold gifts.'

sanskrit: vīrudhaś caiva vṛkṣāṃś ca yajñārthaṃ ca tathauṣadhīḥ paśūṃś caiva tathā medhyān yajñārthāni havīṃṣi ca
english: And the creepers and the trees, and likewise the healing herbs for the sake of sacrifice, and the beasts fit for offering, and the oblations meant for sacrifice.

sanskrit: gṛhasthāśramiṇas tac ca yajñakarma virodhakam tasmād gārhasthyam eveha duṣkaraṃ durlabhaṃ tathā
english: And the work of sacrifice falls hard upon the one who dwells in the householder's order; therefore the household life here is difficult to perform and difficult to attain.

sanskrit: tat saṃprāpya gṛhasthā ye paśudhānyasamanvitāḥ na yajante mahārāja śāśvataṃ teṣu kilbiṣam
english: Those householders who, having gained that state and being well supplied with cattle and grain, yet do not sacrifice—upon them, O great king, rests an everlasting guilt.

sanskrit: svādhyāyayajñā ṛṣayo jñānayajñās tathāpare athāpare mahāyajñān manasaiva vitanvate
english: Some sages make their sacrifice of sacred study, others their sacrifice of knowledge, and yet others perform the great sacrifices by the mind alone.

sanskrit: evaṃ dānasamādhānaṃ mārgam ātiṣṭhato nṛpa dvijāter brahmabhūtasya spṛhayanti divaukasaḥ
english: For the twice-born one who thus treads the path of giving and inward composure, who has become one with Brahman, O king, even the dwellers in heaven yearn.

sanskrit: sa ratnāni vicitrāṇi saṃbhṛtāni tatas tataḥ makheṣv anabhisaṃtyajya nāstikyam abhijalpasi kuṭumbam āsthite tyāgaṃ na paśyāmi narādhipa
english: Without bestowing in sacrifices the varied jewels gathered from here and there, you prattle of unbelief; in one who clings to his household I see no renunciation, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: rājasūyāśvamedheṣu sarvamedheṣu vā punaḥ ya cānye kratavas tāta brāhmaṇair abhipūjitāḥ tair yajasva mahārāja śakro devapatir yathā
english: With the Rājasūya and the Aśvamedha, or again with the Sarvamedha and whatever other rites are honoured by the brāhmaṇas, my dear—worship with these, O great king, as Śakra the lord of the gods once did.

sanskrit: rājñaḥ pramādadoṣeṇa dasyubhiḥ parimuṣyatām aśaraṇyaḥ prajānāṃ yaḥ sa rājā kalir ucyate
english: That king who, through the fault of his own negligence, offers no refuge to his subjects while they are plundered by brigands—he is called a very embodiment of strife, a Kali among kings.

sanskrit: aśvān gāś caiva dāsīś ca kareṇūś ca svalaṃkṛtāḥ grāmāñ janapadāṃś caiva kṣetrāṇi ca gṛhāṇi ca
english: Horses and cattle and serving-women, and richly adorned she-elephants, and villages and provinces, and fields and houses—

sanskrit: apradāya dvijātibhyo mātsaryāviṣṭacetasaḥ vayaṃ te rājakalayo bhaviṣyāmo viśāṃ pate
english: if we do not bestow these upon the twice-born, our minds possessed by selfish envy, we shall become the very dregs and strife of kings, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: adātāro 'śaraṇyāś ca rājakilbiṣabhāginaḥ duḥkhānām eva bhoktāro na sukhānāṃ kadā cana
english: Those who give nothing and afford no refuge, who partake of the guilt that stains kings, are the enjoyers of sorrows alone and never of joys.

sanskrit: aniṣṭvā ca mahāyajñair akṛtvā ca pitṛsvadhām tīrtheṣv anabhisaṃtyajya pravrajiṣyasi ced atha
english: If, without having worshipped with the great sacrifices, without having offered the libation to the ancestors, and without having bestowed gifts at the holy fords, you shall then go forth as a wanderer—

sanskrit: chinnābhram iva gantāsi vilayaṃ māruteritam lokayor ubhayor bhraṣṭo hy antarāle vyavasthitaḥ
english: you will go to your dissolution like a sundered cloud driven by the wind, fallen from both worlds and left suspended in the void between them.

sanskrit: antar bahiś ca yat kiṃ cin manovyāsaṅgakārakam parityajya bhavet tyāgī na yo hitvā pratiṣṭhate
english: Whatever, within or without, breeds attachment in the mind—by relinquishing that does one become a renouncer, not by merely forsaking his place and going elsewhere.

sanskrit: etasmin vartamānasya vidhau vipraniṣevite brāhmaṇasya mahārāja nocchittir vidyate kva cit
english: For the brāhmaṇa who treads this ordinance practised by the wise, O great king, there is found no ruin anywhere at all.

sanskrit: nihatya śatrūṃs tarasā samṛddhān; śakro yathā daityabalāni saṃkhye kaḥ pārtha śocen nirataḥ svadharme; pūrvaiḥ smṛte pārthiva śiṣṭajuṣṭe
english: Having swiftly struck down his flourishing foes, as Śakra struck the hosts of the Daityas in battle—who, O Pārtha, devoted to his own duty, should grieve over a path remembered by the ancients and cherished by the virtuous, O lord of the earth?

sanskrit: kṣātreṇa dharmeṇa parākrameṇa; jitvā mahīṃ mantravidbhyaḥ pradāya nākasya pṛṣṭhe 'si narendra gantā; na śocitavyaṃ bhavatādya pārtha
english: Having conquered the earth by the kṣatriya's law and by your valour, and bestowed it upon those who know the sacred verses, you shall go to the summit of heaven, O lord of men; there is nothing for you to grieve over this day, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: sahadeva uvāca na bāhyaṃ dravyam utsṛjya siddhir bhavati bhārata śārīraṃ dravyam utsṛjya siddhir bhavati vā na vā
english: Sahadeva said: Perfection does not come by casting away outward possessions, O descendant of Bharata; by casting away the possession that is the body, perfection may come, or it may not.

sanskrit: bāhyadravyavimuktasya śārīreṣu ca gṛdhyataḥ yo dharmo yat sukhaṃ vā syād dviṣatāṃ tat tathāstu naḥ
english: Whatever merit or whatever happiness belongs to one who is free of outward possessions yet still craves the things of the body—let that fall to the lot of those who hate us.

sanskrit: śārīraṃ dravyam utsṛjya pṛthivīm anuśāsataḥ yo dharmo yat sukhaṃ vā syāt suhṛdāṃ tat tathāstu naḥ
english: Whatever merit or whatever happiness belongs to one who casts away even the possession that is the body while he governs the earth—let that fall to the lot of our friends.

sanskrit: dvyakṣaras tu bhaven mṛtyus tryakṣaraṃ brahma śāśvatam mameti ca bhaven mṛtyur na mameti ca śāśvatam
english: Of two syllables is Death, mṛtyu; of three syllables is the eternal Brahman, śāśvatam. 'Mine' is Death; 'not mine' is the eternal.

sanskrit: brahmamṛtyū ca tau rājann ātmany eva samāśritau adṛśyamānau bhūtāni yodhayetām asaṃśayam
english: Both Brahman and Death, O king, abide together within the self alone; unseen, they wage war over all beings—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: avināśo 'sya sattvasya niyato yadi bhārata bhittvā śarīraṃ bhūtānāṃ na hiṃsā pratipatsyate
english: If the indestructibility of this living essence is a fixed truth, O descendant of Bharata, then in cleaving the bodies of beings no real injury is incurred.

sanskrit: athāpi ca sahotpattiḥ sattvasya pralayas tathā naṣṭe śarīre naṣṭaṃ syād vṛthā ca syāt kriyāpathaḥ
english: But if, on the other hand, the essence arises together with the body and so too dissolves with it, then when the body perishes it would perish as well, and the whole path of ritual action would be in vain.

sanskrit: tasmād ekāntam utsṛjya pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraiś ca yaḥ panthā niṣevitaḥ sadbhiḥ sa niṣevyo vijānatā
english: Therefore, casting aside this extreme view, the path that was followed by the ancients and by those still earlier, by the good—that path should be followed by the one who truly knows.

sanskrit: labdhvāpi pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ sahasthāvarajaṅgamām na bhuṅkte yo nṛpaḥ samyaṅ niṣphalaṃ tasya jīvitam
english: The king who, even having won the whole earth with all that stands still and all that moves, does not rightly enjoy it—his life is fruitless.

sanskrit: atha vā vasato rājan vane vanyena jīvataḥ dravyeṣu yasya mamatā mṛtyor āsye sa vartate
english: And on the other hand, O king, of one who dwells in the forest and lives upon its wild fare, if he still feels the sense of 'mine' toward possessions, he abides within the very jaws of death.

sanskrit: bāhyābhyantarabhūtānāṃ svabhāvaṃ paśya bhārata ye tu paśyanti tadbhāvaṃ mucyante mahato bhayāt
english: Behold the true nature of things both outward and inward, O descendant of Bharata; those who perceive that nature are released from the great fear.

sanskrit: bhavān pitā bhavān mātā bhavān bhrātā bhavān guruḥ duḥkhapralāpān ārtasya tasmān me kṣantum arhasi
english: You are my father, you my mother, you my brother, you my teacher; therefore you should forgive me, a man in distress, the grief-stricken lamentations I have uttered.

sanskrit: tathyaṃ vā yadi vātathyaṃ yan mayaitat prabhāṣitam tad viddhi pṛthivīpāla bhaktyā bharatasattama
english: Whether what I have here spoken be true or untrue, know it to be spoken out of devotion, O protector of the earth, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca avyāharati kaunteye dharmarāje yudhiṣṭhire bhrātṝṇāṃ bruvatāṃ tāṃs tān vividhān vedaniścayān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, the king of righteousness, kept silent, and his brothers were declaring their various certainties drawn from the Veda—

sanskrit: mahābhijanasaṃpannā śrīmaty āyatalocanā abhyabhāṣata rājendraṃ draupadī yoṣitāṃ varā
english: Draupadī, sprung from a great lineage, radiant and large-eyed, the foremost of women, addressed that lord of kings.

sanskrit: āsīnam ṛṣabhaṃ rājñāṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritam siṃhaśārdūlasadṛśair vāraṇair iva yūthapam
english: He sat there, a bull among kings, encircled by his brothers who were like lions and tigers—even as the leader of a herd is encircled by elephants.

sanskrit: abhimānavatī nityaṃ viśeṣeṇa yudhiṣṭhire lālitā satataṃ rājñā dharmajñā dharmadarśinī
english: Ever proud, and most of all toward Yudhiṣṭhira, forever cherished by the king, she who knew righteousness and beheld righteousness—

sanskrit: āmantrya vipulaśroṇī sāmnā paramavalgunā bhartāram abhisaṃprekṣya tato vacanam abravīt
english: the broad-hipped one, addressing her lord with words exceedingly gentle and conciliatory, and gazing upon him, then spoke.

sanskrit: ime te bhrātaraḥ pārtha śuṣyanta stokakā iva vāvāśyamānās tiṣṭhanti na cainān abhinandase
english: These brothers of yours, O Pārtha, stand here parched like the cātaka birds, crying out again and again, yet you give them no answering gladness.

sanskrit: nandayaitān mahārāja mattān iva mahādvipān upapannena vākyena satataṃ duḥkhabhāginaḥ
english: Gladden them, O great king, who like great rutting elephants have long been partakers of sorrow, with words that befit the occasion.

sanskrit: kathaṃ dvaitavane rājan pūrvam uktvā tathā vacaḥ bhrātṝn etān sma sahitāñ śītavātātapārditān
english: How is it, O king, that in the Dvaita forest you once spoke such words to these your brothers, gathered together and tormented by cold, wind, and heat—

sanskrit: vayaṃ duryodhanaṃ hatvā mṛdhe bhokṣyāma medinīm saṃpūrṇāṃ sarvakāmānām āhave vijayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: 'Having slain Duryodhana in battle, we shall enjoy the earth, full of all that the heart desires'—we who longed for victory in the fray?

sanskrit: virathāṃś ca rathān kṛtvā nihatya ca mahāgajān saṃstīrya ca rathair bhūmiṃ sasādibhir ariṃdamāḥ
english: 'Having unhorsed the chariot-warriors and slain the great elephants, and strewn the earth with chariots and their riders, O subduers of foes—'

sanskrit: yajatāṃ vividhair yajñaiḥ samṛddhair āptadakṣiṇaiḥ vanavāsakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati sukhāya naḥ
english: 'We shall worship with manifold sacrifices, abundant and supplied with fitting gifts; and the sorrow wrought by our forest-dwelling shall turn to our joy.'

sanskrit: ity etān evam uktvā tvaṃ svayaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara katham adya punar vīra vinihaṃsi manāṃsy uta
english: Having yourself spoken to them in this very wise, O foremost of the upholders of duty, how is it, O hero, that today you crush their spirits again?

sanskrit: na klībo vasudhāṃ bhuṅkte na klībo dhanam aśnute na klībasya gṛhe putrā matsyāḥ paṅka ivāsate
english: No weakling enjoys the earth, no weakling partakes of wealth; in the weakling's house no sons abide—they perish like fish in the mud.

sanskrit: nādaṇḍaḥ kṣatriyo bhāti nādaṇḍo bhūtim aśnute nādaṇḍasya prajā rājñaḥ sukham edhanti bhārata
english: The kṣatriya who wields no rod of chastisement does not shine; without the rod he gains no prosperity; without the rod of the king, his subjects do not thrive in happiness, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: mitratā sarvabhūteṣu dānam adhyayanaṃ tapaḥ brāhmaṇasyaiṣa dharmaḥ syān na rājño rājasattama
english: Friendliness toward all beings, giving, sacred study, and austerity—this would be the duty of the brāhmaṇa, not of the king, O best of kings.

sanskrit: asatāṃ pratiṣedhaś ca satāṃ ca paripālanam eṣa rājñāṃ paro dharmaḥ samare cāpalāyanam
english: The restraint of the wicked and the protection of the good—this is the supreme duty of kings, and not to flee in battle.

sanskrit: yasmin kṣamā ca krodhaś ca dānādāne bhayābhaye nigrahānugrahau cobhau sa vai dharmavid ucyate
english: He in whom dwell forbearance and anger, giving and withholding, fear and fearlessness, and both punishment and grace—he indeed is called one who knows what is right.

sanskrit: na śrutena na dānena na sāntvena na cejyayā tvayeyaṃ pṛthivī labdhā notkocena tathāpy uta
english: Not by learning, nor by giving, nor by conciliation, nor by sacrifice, nor yet by bribery was this earth won by you.

sanskrit: yat tad balam amitrāṇāṃ tathā vīrasamudyatam hastyaśvarathasaṃpannaṃ tribhir aṅgair mahattaram
english: That mighty host of your enemies, raised up by heroes, abounding in elephants, horses, and chariots, the greater for its three divisions—

sanskrit: rakṣitaṃ droṇakarṇābhyām aśvatthāmnā kṛpeṇa ca tat tvayā nihataṃ vīra tasmād bhuṅkṣva vasuṃdharām
english: guarded by Droṇa and Karṇa, by Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa—that host you struck down, O hero; therefore enjoy the earth.

sanskrit: jambūdvīpo mahārāja nānājanapadāyutaḥ tvayā puruṣaśārdūla daṇḍena mṛditaḥ prabho
english: Jambūdvīpa, O great king, thronged with its many provinces, was crushed by you, O tiger among men, by the rod of chastisement, O lord.

sanskrit: jambūdvīpena sadṛśaḥ krauñcadvīpo narādhipa apareṇa mahāmeror daṇḍena mṛditas tvayā
english: Krauñcadvīpa, the equal of Jambūdvīpa, O ruler of men, lying to the west of the great Meru, was crushed by you with the rod.

sanskrit: krauñcadvīpena sadṛśaḥ śākadvīpo narādhipa pūrveṇa tu mahāmeror daṇḍena mṛditas tvayā
english: Śākadvīpa, the equal of Krauñcadvīpa, O ruler of men, lying to the east of the great Meru, was crushed by you with the rod.

sanskrit: uttareṇa mahāmeroḥ śākadvīpena saṃmitaḥ bhadrāśvaḥ puruṣavyāghra daṇḍena mṛditas tvayā
english: Bhadrāśva, equal in measure to Śākadvīpa and lying to the north of the great Meru, O tiger among men, was crushed by you with the rod.

sanskrit: dvīpāś ca sāntaradvīpā nānājanapadālayāḥ vigāhya sāgaraṃ vīra daṇḍena mṛditās tvayā
english: And the continents together with their lesser islands, the dwelling-places of many peoples—plunging across the ocean, O hero, you crushed them with the rod.

sanskrit: etāny apratimāni tvaṃ kṛtvā karmāṇi bhārata na prīyase mahārāja pūjyamāno dvijātibhiḥ
english: Having wrought these matchless deeds, O descendant of Bharata, you take no joy, O great king, though you are honoured by the twice-born.
